guinee.intro: Beaches and islands on the Atlantic, cool highlands in the Fouta Djallon, waterfalls, forests and a living culture: Guinea brings all of this together in one country.
guinee.whyTitle: A destination that is still authentic, a few hours away by plane

reasons.title: Beaches & islands
reasons.text: Bel-Air and its 7 km of coconut palms, the Loos Islands off Conakry, the mangroves of the Lower Coast.

reasons.title: Cool highlands
reasons.text: The Fouta Djallon and Mount Loura (1,515 m), for hiking and panoramic views.

reasons.title: Waterfalls & nature
reasons.text: The Nguilo Falls, the Mount Dixinn falls, the natural pools of Dubréka.

reasons.title: Culture & memory
reasons.text: The Fula heritage of the Fouta, the Susu culture of the coast, the memorial sites of Boffa and Fotoba.

guinee.regionsText: We are starting with Lower Guinea and Middle Guinea. Upper Guinea and Forest Guinea will follow at a later stage.

regions.title: Lower Guinea
regions.text: Beaches, islands, mangroves. Susu people, Susu language.

regions.title: Middle Guinea
regions.text: Highlands, waterfalls. Fula people, Pular language.

destinations.title: Mali & the Fouta Djallon
destinations.text: Mount Loura, Nguilo Falls, Koumba rocks.

destinations.alt: Boat on the sea at sunset
destinations.title: Loos Islands
destinations.text: Lively Kassa, wild Tamara, peaceful Roume.

destinations.title: Bel-Air, Sobane & Kitikata
destinations.text: 7 km of fine sand, nights under the stars, drumming.

destinations.title: Dubréka
destinations.text: Canoes, natural pools, Mount Dixinn falls.

cultures.title: The Fula Fouta Djallon
cultures.text: Heart of the Fouta Djallon imamate in the 18th century: Islam, herding and hospitality remain essential there. Pular is spoken.

cultures.title: The Susu coast
cultures.text: Lower Guinea is largely populated by the Susu. Fishing, farming and life to the rhythm of the tides.

cultures.title: Places of memory
cultures.text: Boffa, Dubréka and Fotoba preserve remains of the slave trade and the colonial period.

essentials.title: When to go
essentials.text: The dry season is the best time for swimming, boat crossings and hiking.

essentials.title: Health
essentials.text: Certificate required on entry for travellers from at-risk countries, recommended for everyone. See a doctor 4 to 6 weeks before.

essentials.title: Gateway: Conakry
essentials.text: The capital (3,407,327 inhabitants, preliminary 2025 census) is the starting point for the whole coast.

guinee.ctaTitle: Plan your trip to Guinea with our local guides

gallery: Traveller facing the panorama of the highlands
fouta.historyP1: In the 18th century, the Fouta Djallon was the heart of a Fula theocratic state, the Imamate of Fouta Djallon. This heritage explains the importance of Islam, herding and hospitality in the region.
fouta.historyP2: Mali once enjoyed a period of popularity with visitors, with leisure spots and a hotel named after Mount Loura. Today the sites remain largely undeveloped, which is what makes them authentic.

sites.title: Mount Loura, the “Lady of Mali”
sites.text: Highest point of the Fouta. Hiking, photography and village encounters.

sites.title: Nguilo Falls
sites.text: Steep trail, a half-day with a local guide.

sites.title: Koumba rocks & Balaki hill
sites.text: Discover the rocky landscape of the urban commune.

fouta.dayPlaceholder: [Details of the stage, stops and accommodation to be confirmed by the agency.]
fouta.accessText: Plan for a 4×4, a local guide and confirmed accommodation. We organise everything for you.
fouta.healthText: Meningitis vaccine advised from November to June in the north and centre. Yellow fever required on entry. See a doctor 4 to 6 weeks before.

loos.intro: An archipelago off the capital: red-sand beaches, coves, fishermen and history. The perfect weekend getaway.
loos.historyTitle: The “Ilhas dos Ídolos” of the Portuguese navigators
loos.historyP1: The name Loos comes from the Portuguese Ilhas dos Ídolos, the “islands of idols”. Occupied by the British in the 19th century, they were ceded to France in 1904.
loos.historyP2: On Kassa island, the remains of the Fotoba penitentiary recall the colonial period. A guided visit helps understand this past before heading to the beaches.
loos.historyImageAlt: Sea horizon seen from an island

islands.text: The most visited island: beach restaurants, music at weekends and the historic site of Fotoba.
The largest island, with its red-sand beaches and Alcatraz rock, a refuge for seabirds.
A small, peaceful island, perfect for reading, swimming and enjoying the calm away from the city.

loos.whatsappMessage: Hello ETHNIKA, I would like a quote for a Loos Islands getaway.

tips.title: When to go
tips.text: In the dry season (November to April): calmer sea and safer crossings.

tips.title: What to bring
tips.text: Sunscreen, hat, bottled water, a waterproof bag for the crossing.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: Life jacket mandatory in the canoe. Swim carefully and ask about the currents.

basseCote.intro: Endless beaches, mangroves, canoe rides on rivers and places of memory. A coast largely inhabited by the Susu, a few hours from Conakry.
basseCote.boffaText: On the banks of the Fatala river, Boffa has kept its old port, one of the first churches in the country and sites linked to the slave trade. A powerful stop to understand the history of Guinea.
basseCote.belAirTitle: 7 km of fine sand and coconut palms
basseCote.belAirText: One of the most beautiful beaches in the country. Swimming, sunrise walks, grilled fish and nights to the sound of the waves.

villages.title: Sobane
villages.text: A fishing village by the ocean. Calm, sunsets and a warm welcome.

villages.title: Kitikata
villages.text: Nights under the stars, drumming and village life to the rhythm of the tides.

villages.title: Lake Koba
villages.alt: Reflections on a body of water
villages.text: A lake surrounded by greenery, for a nature day, picnic and birdwatching.

basseCote.dubrekaText: North of Conakry, some sites are reached by canoe. Natural pools, the Bondabon site and the Mount Dixinn falls for a refreshing day out.
basseCote.dubrekaImageAlt: River lined with vegetation and a canoe
basseCote.conakryText: For an afternoon without leaving the city, before or after a flight.
basseCote.ctaText: Transport, accommodation, meals and local guide included. Departure from Conakry. Best season: November to April.

seasons.title: Dry season
seasons.text: Best period: beaches, crossings to the islands, hiking in the Fouta.

seasons.title: Rainy season
seasons.text: Very green landscapes and abundant waterfalls, but tracks and sea are more difficult.

infos.formalitiesText: Passport valid for more than 6 months after your return, a visa depending on your nationality [TO BE CHECKED with the embassy or the official portal], and an international certificate of vaccination against yellow fever.

vaccines.name: Yellow fever
vaccines.note: Required for travellers aged 9 months and over coming from an at-risk country, recommended for everyone. At least 10 days before departure, valid for life.

vaccines.name: Hepatitis A and B
vaccines.note: Transmitted through water, food or blood.

vaccines.name: Meningitis
vaccines.note: Especially from November to June, in the north and centre.

vaccines.name: Typhoid, polio, boosters
vaccines.note: Update diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, measles.

vaccines.name: Rabies, cholera
vaccines.note: Long stays, remote areas, contact with animals.

infos.malariaText: Present throughout the country, all year round. Preventive treatment is generally advised: ask your doctor.

daily.title: Water
daily.text: Sealed bottled water, no ice of unknown origin.

daily.title: Sun
daily.text: Sunscreen, hat, and stay well hydrated.

daily.title: First aid & insurance

daily.title: Swimming
daily.text: Watch out for currents; ask your guide for advice.

money.text: Guinean franc; bring cash outside Conakry.
A local SIM card is easy to get with a passport.
French is the official language; Susu, Pular and Malinké are widely spoken.
